summary: Full texts confirm both trials used Sunfiber PHGG from Taiyo Kagaku. In IBS (121 randomized, 6 g/day for 12 weeks) bloating and bloating+gas improved versus placebo, but overall severity, quality of life, pain and stool frequency did not, with heavy differential attrition. In healthy adults with loose stools (5 g/day) stool form improved at weeks 7 and 11, with no change in frequency (maker-funded). Both get eligible contexts with those mixed directions recorded; the existing Sunfiber-only digestive applicability is unchanged.

population.description: 44 healthy Japanese adults aged 20-49 with loose stools (diagnosed IBS excluded), selected from 88 screened; 22 per arm after a 4-week run-in.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group single-centre trial, 12 weeks plus follow-up; primary endpoints stool form (Bristol) and frequency; conducted by a CRO on consignment from Taiyo Kagaku.

dose.administration_frequency: One 5 g sachet daily for 12 weeks.

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC6769658): Methods (design, Sunfiber provided by Taiyo Kagaku, 5 g/day dose rationale, participants, endpoints), Results stool form paragraph, Funding and Conflicts of Interest.

outcomes.name: Primary stool form: Bristol score lower than placebo at weeks 7 and 11 (p<0.05) with significant time-by-treatment interaction (p<0.05).

limitations: Small, single dose; 5 g PHGGnot 5 g dietary fiber; brand correspondence mustbeverified.
Funded by Taiyo Kagaku; three authors are Taiyo Kagaku employees. Stool-form benefit was intermittent (weeks 7 and 11) with modest power.
Returned A023 date-only restriction withdrawn; assessed on verified full text. Credit limited to selective digestive outcomes under the existing Sunfiber-only applicability.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

population.description: 121 adults with Rome III IBS (all subtypes) randomized at two Israeli centres; 108 in the reported intention-to-treat analysis (49 PHGG, 59 placebo); dropout 22.45% PHGG vs 49.15% placebo.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo (maltodextrin)-controlled trial: 2-week run-in, 12 weeks treatment, 4 weeks follow-up; primary endpoints changes in journal symptom scores, Francis severity and IBS-QOL.

dose.administration_frequency: One sachet dissolved in a glass of water daily: 3 g/day for 7 days, then 6 g/day for 11 weeks.
dose.reported_regimen: 3 g/day for the first seven days, then 6 g/day for eleven weeks; one titrated active regimen over twelve weeks, not two independent arms.

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC4744437): Methods (design paragraph naming Sunfiber by Taiyo Kagaku, dosing, outcomes, statistics), Results Table 2 paragraphs, competing interests.

co_therapies: Usual diet continued; probiotics and prebiotics not allowed.

outcomes.name: Primary journal bloating score improved vs placebo (-4.1 vs -1.2, P=0.03) and bloating+gas (-4.3 vs -1.12, P=0.035), lasting 4 weeks after stopping.
Primary Francis IBS severity and quality of life, abdominal pain and stool frequency: no effect.

limitations: Titratedregimen, not 6 g throughout; noall IBS symptom benefit.
The 3 g lead-in is titration within the 6 g/day protocol, not evidence for a separate 3 g efficacy arm.
Substantial differential attrition and baseline severity imbalance (PHGG group more severe). Benefit is selective for bloating/gas.
Returned A023 date-only restriction withdrawn; assessed on verified full text. Credit limited to selective digestive outcomes under the existing Sunfiber-only applicability.

source_receipts.title_fetched: Effect of Repeated Consumption of Partially Hydrolyzed Guar Gum on Fecal Characteristics and Gut Microbiota: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, and Parallel-Group Clinical Trial.
Randomized clinical study: Partially hydrolyzed guar gum (PHGG) versus placebo in the treatment of patients with irritable bowel syndrome.

freshness_search.database: PubMed (NCBI E-utilities esearch, sort=pub_date, retmax=60; titles via esummary, abstracts via efetch)
freshness_search.query: ("partially hydrolyzed guar gum" OR "partially hydrolysed guar gum" OR PHGG OR Sunfiber) AND (irritable bowel OR bowel OR stool OR constipation OR diarrhea OR bloating OR gastrointestinal) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt] OR randomized controlled trial[pt])

supplementary_queries.query: (guar[tiab]) AND (irritable bowel OR constipation OR stool OR bowel) AND (meta-analysis[pt] OR systematic review[pt] OR meta-analysis[ti])

freshness_search.screening_rule: Kept oral PHGG RCTs or syntheses newer than the credited trials (2016, 2019) on bowel/IBS outcomes. Excluded enteral-nutrition, oral-rehydration and post-surgical formula studies and other gums.

read.title: Natural products for the management of diarrhea: a systematic review of clinical efficacy, safety, and certainty of evidence.
read.finding: 2026 SR, 10 studies including PHGG: most reported improvements in diarrhea outcomes, but GRADE certainty was low to very low. No pooled PHGG estimate.

read.title: Effectiveness of Partially Hydrolyzed Guar Gum in Reducing Constipation in Long Term Care Facility Residents: A Randomized Single-Blinded Placebo-Controlled Trial.
read.finding: 2022 single-blind RCT, 52 long-term-care residents (mean age 83.9) with chronic constipation, PHGG 5 g/day vs water for 4 weeks: no difference in bowel frequency or Bristol stool form; less laxative use in weeks 3-4. The abstract does not name the product brand.

read.title: Effects of a prebiotic formulation on the composition of the faecal microbiota of people with functional constipation.
read.finding: 2024 exploratory analysis of a 21-day RCT (61 adults, functional constipation) of a PHGG + acacia gum formulation: microbiome outcomes only. Multi-ingredient, so not applicable.

freshness_search.conclusion: confirms: no newer synthesis pools PHGG for the credited outcomes. The newer trials are in a different population (frail constipated elderly, null for stool form) or test a multi-ingredient product, at low certainty. The mixed directions already recorded for 26855665 and 31509971 stand.
